requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Select a topic related to the United States that is currently in the news. Describe to your counselor what is happening. Explain how today's events are related to or affected by the events and values of America's past. misconception_pool.misconception: The Star-Spangled Banner became the official United States national anthem immediately after Francis Scott Key wrote it in 1814.
misconception_pool.fact: Key wrote the poem during the War of 1812, but Congress did not make The Star-Spangled Banner the official anthem until 1931.

misconception_pool.misconception: Francis Bellamy included the phrase under God when he first published the Pledge of Allegiance in 1892.
misconception_pool.fact: Bellamy's 1892 text did not include the words under God; Congress added that phrase by statute on June 14, 1954.

misconception_pool.misconception: E Pluribus Unum has always been the sole official national motto of the United States under federal law.
misconception_pool.fact: E Pluribus Unum appeared on the Great Seal in 1782, while Congress established In God We Trust as the official motto in 1956.

misconception_pool.misconception: The Flag Act of 1818 adds a new stripe and a new star to the United States flag whenever a new state joins the Union.
misconception_pool.fact: The Flag Act of 1818 fixed the flag at thirteen stripes for the original colonies and adds one star on the fourth of July after admission.
